name: Shoal Ingest
description: Watches one or more drop folders. New media is identified from its release name and the server's own metadata providers, renamed to Jellyfin's naming standard (with provider IDs) and moved, with its subtitles, into the destination library for its kind. Release clutter is quarantined and purged after a retention period. Anything that can't be identified confidently waits on the plugin page for a decision.
overview: Watch drop folders and file new media into your libraries, correctly named.

versions.changelog: 0.1.8-alpha: review fixes. Libraries on a whole drive can be filed into; Jellyfin's metadata and transcode folders are protected; folder links and unreadable releases are handled. Quarantine never touches date folders Ingest didn't create, and "Quarantine release" is crash-safe and logged. Recovery only touches Ingest's own temporary files, a full disk after a move no longer splits a release, a hung network share can't stall filing, and choices on the review screen are checked against what the page showed.
0.1.7-alpha: a Quarantine section on the plugin page shows what is in quarantine (by date, per release, with file sizes) and the day each folder is deleted.

0.1.6-alpha: the plugin family is now called Shoal (this plugin shows as "Shoal Ingest"; settings and data are unchanged). Build hardening: pinned Jellyfin packages, locked restores, build-provenance attestation.

0.1.5-alpha: an offline library share is never recreated on the local disk (the release waits and retries); a provider outage is retried automatically and pauses identification instead of stranding releases in review; searches are cached; titles in any script match; decisions made during planning are kept; safer file names; only the folders filed into are refreshed; state-file errors are handled; quieter, more private logs and a trimmed action log.

0.1.4-alpha: safety release. Symbolic links are never followed; provider ids are validated and every move is checked to stay inside its library or the quarantine; unsafe watch and quarantine folders are refused, and the purge only deletes folders Ingest created; downloads still being written are not mistaken for finished ones; moves are crash-safe and all-or-nothing; one unreadable folder no longer stops the others.

name: Shoal Subtitles
description: Finds subtitles for videos that are missing them (OpenSubtitles through Jellyfin, subtitles embedded in the file, other providers), scores the candidates, checks them against the actual audio and synchronises their timing. Speech-to-text runs locally by default (built-in Whisper), with optional cloud services. Every change is reversible.
overview: Find, check and synchronise subtitles so they match the audio.

versions.changelog: 0.4.0-alpha: completes the first stage. SubDL as an extra subtitle source (with a free key; the right episode is taken from season packs). Opt-in checking of subtitle tracks inside video files (a corrected copy is added beside the video when a track is out of time). Deepgram credit balance on the settings page, with a guard that swaps an Admin key for a transcription-only key. A helper that finds a local speech-to-text service or shows how to run one.

0.3.0-alpha: paid speech-to-text (Deepgram, OpenAI) can be used by the nightly runs within your monthly limit, in your currency. Every call is priced from the providers' published prices, reserved against the limit and recorded; a call that would go over the limit, or whose cost can't be worked out, isn't made. The settings page shows this month's spending.

0.2.0-alpha: built-in speech-to-text. Once you allow it, whisper.cpp and a speech model are downloaded from this project's releases, checked against checksums built into the plugin, and run on the server's CPU. Also: undo is safe after another tool replaces a subtitle, large libraries are checked once each, downloads and huge files are capped, Apply/Undo errors are shown, downloads default to 10 a day and stop when the provider's allowance is used up, and forced-only tracks no longer count as having subtitles.

0.1.0-alpha, the first release: checks subtitle files beside films and episodes against the audio every day and fixes their timing (shifts and PAL frame-rate changes), first for free by matching line starts, then with a local speech-to-text service for the unclear cases; cleans adverts and bad timing; finds subtitles for videos that have none through Jellyfin's subtitle providers, adding one only if it fits the audio. Every change can be undone. The built-in speech-to-text and paid services in automatic runs are not in this release yet.
